OpenAI updated the recently redesigned Mac version of the ChatGPT app, making it easier for users to access their conversations again. Here are the details.

OpenAI responds to the main complaints triggered by the redesign of its Mac app

Last Thursday, OpenAI launched a brand-new Mac version of the ChatGPT app, integrating ChatGPT, Codex and the newly announced Work agent on the same platform, while renaming the original app as ChatGPT Classic.

The overhaul sparked controversy, mainly for two reasons: first, the new app replaced the original native Mac client with a bulky Electron-based program. Second, its interface was confusing — a prominent drop-down menu was used to switch between Codex and Work, while the standard Chat conversation function was demoted to an inconspicuous button that, when opened, only displayed a floating window with no access to users' existing conversation history or Projects.

Shortly after the update was released, users flocked to OpenAI's community forum and X platform to protest the baffling change. The following day, Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, who has been leading OpenAI's efforts to merge ChatGPT and Codex into a unified "super app," acknowledged the criticism and pledged to restore conversations and Projects to the sidebar, clarify the distinction between ChatGPT Work and Codex, and address other usability issues.

OpenAI has now updated the new ChatGPT app in response to some of the complaints, with the most pressing being the inability to directly access conversations. Users can now switch back and forth between Chat and Work via a prominent toggle at the top of the window, while a drop-down menu in the sidebar allows them to choose between the standard version of ChatGPT or Codex.

9to5Mac's take

Although the ChatGPT app's interface remains confusing, users who simply want to use ChatGPT can finally chat with the chatbot as they did before.

Still, this baffling misstep — relegating ChatGPT to a secondary feature behind Work and Codex, coupled with the switch to Electron — suggests OpenAI is more focused on competing with Anthropic than on delivering a quality user experience. Thank goodness ChatGPT Classic is still around; let's hope it stays that way.
